cards.front: Following pediatric both bone forearm fracture , should you place the patient in a short-arm or long-arm cast? Short-arm
cards.extra: As stated in the articles below, short arm casts for distal both bone forearm fractures are as effective as long arm casts; however, short arm casts have fewer complications associated with them. Paneru et al. (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC2866844/) randomized 42 children aged 4-12 to an above-elbow group and 43 to a below-elbow group. They found that pain and swelling on the next day and one week after reduction was significantly higher in the above-elbow group. As well, patients in the above-elbow group were more likely to undergo a re-manipulation than the below-elbow group (9.5% vs. 2.3%, p=0.173). Webb et al. (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16391244/) performed an RCT comparing short arm and long arm plaster casts for displaced distal both bone forearm fractures. They concluded that a well-molded short arm cast was equally as effective as a long-arm cast, and interfered less with daily activity. They stressed the need for proper cast molding, indicated by a lower cast index. The ideal cast index is less than 0.8.

cards.front: Posterior cervical fusion is the treatment of choice for symptomatic cervical pseudoarthrosis following anterior cervical diskectomy and fusion .
cards.extra: Even though there are increased complications with the posterior approach, there are substantially increased rates of fusion with lower revision surgery rate. *The study by Carreon et al (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16517386/) is a retrospective case series that compared posterior cervical fusion versus revision anterior surgery for the treatment of a symptomatic pseudoarthrosis. They found a second revision surgery for persistent nonunion was required in 44% of patients in the anterior revision group, and only 2% of the patients in the posterior revision group. Therefore, they argue that despite increased blood loss, longer postoperative hospitalization, and an increased complication rate, posterior cervical fusion is a better treatment option due to higher fusion rates and a decrease in revision surgery rates.
